name: Wavetable crossfade position + morph/PWM-style shaping
goal: Build evolving WT pads by smoothly crossfading through table frames (not hard digital switches), modulating table position from LFO/mod sources, and using morph-style wave shapers (pulse-width-like morph on squares, mirror/stretch/narrow toward filter-like thinning, optional vintage bit-step) as a portable delta beyond basic WT-position-only pads.

source.title: You Won’t Believe What the Modwave Can Do With Wavetables!

prerequisites: Wavetable oscillator with position/crossfade and optional morph/wave-shaping modes; LFO or mod matrix; filter + FX

inputs.name: crossfade
inputs.description: Smooth interpolate between frames vs hard switch

outputs.name: wt_morph_pad
outputs.description: Position-modulated WT pad with optional morph shaping

constraints: Ground every step in the source YouTube-provided Show-transcript text; do not invent UI paths or numeric settings not stated there.
Original synthesis / signal-flow only — map brand UI to portable osc/filter/env/LFO/FX modules for Traveler-inspired or Web Audio hybrid; never rip presets, wavetables, or samples.
Prefer transferable parameter relationships over vendor-specific preset or bank names.
Not affiliated with the plugin/hardware vendors named in the source video; recreate with comparable modules.
Delta vs traveler-walkthrough-wavetable-morph-filter-motion / digital-wt-morph: emphasizes smooth crossfade vs hard switch, morph/PWM/mirror/narrow shaping, and vintage bit-step color—not FX order.

steps.action: Load a multi-frame wavetable (e.g. saw→triangle→square→sine family). Enable smooth crossfade/interpolation between frames so in-between waves are audible; contrast with crossfade=0 hard switching for sharp digital hops.
steps.expect: Smooth timbral blend vs stepped jumps

steps.action: Assign LFO or other mod source to wavetable position/crossfade amount for evolving motion; keep depth musical for pads.

Engage morph-style shaping: on pulse/square-like frames, morph acts like PWM; explore mirror, mirror-stretch/wavefold-like, narrowing (toward high-pass thinness) and window-narrow (toward low-pass softening).
Optional vintage digital character: apply bit-resolution / stepped vintage modes (e.g. 8-bit buzzing overtones) and LFO them lightly for early-digital WT flavor through an analog-style filter.
Finish with ladder/LP filter + envelopes, then EQ→chorus→delay→reverb for cinematic space. Prefer original/free tables—do not dump proprietary banks.

verification: Crossfade on yields intermediate waveforms; off yields hard switches
At least one morph mode (PWM/mirror/narrow/vintage) audibly changes harmonics
